text:
alex.m: Heads-up, getting a spike of TLS handshake failures for dedicated /private-api endpoints in eu-west-1. errors in prometheus: tls_handshake_failures + ALB 502-like client disconnects.

maya.k: saw the alert, digging. any pattern on client IPs or UA?

alex.m: mostly mobile clients and a few partner servers. ALB access logs show connection closed at TLS handshake stage. example ALB log line:
`2026-04-03T09:12:03.123Z app/redwood-eu/abcdef 1.2.3.4:54321 10.0.5.12:443 0.000 0.005 0.000 502 502 0 0 "GET /private-api/health HTTP/1.1" "curl/7.68.0" - - - - TLSAlert \n`

ryan: are we terminating TLS on the ALB or passing through to the ingress?

alex.m: for these dedicated endpoints we moved to TLS passthrough (NLB -> target group -> nginx) so backend handles mTLS. recently toggled proxy-protocol on the target group to preserve client IPs.

maya.k: ohh. did nginx get configured to accept PROXY v2 header? IIRC TLS passthrough + proxy protocol mismatch will corrupt the ClientHello.

sanjay: confirmed - target group had proxy_protocol enabled but the ingress pods were not using a proxy-protocol aware listener. nginx is seeing garbage bytes before TLS ClientHello.

alex.m: that would produce TLS decode errors. can someone tcpdump on a pod to confirm?

ryan: running quick tcpdump on node ->
```
# tcpdump -s 0 -w /tmp/tls.pcap 'tcp port 443 and host 10.0.5.12'
# hexdump -C /tmp/tls.pcap | head
00000000  50 52 4f 58 59 20 54 43  50 34 20 31 2e 32 2e 33  |PROXY TCP4 1.2.3|
00000010  20 31 30 2e 30 2e 35 2e 31  32 20 30 00 00 00 00  | 10.0.5.12 0....|
```

ryan: there it is — `PROXY` header in front of TLS bytes. nginx then tries to parse ClientHello and fails.

maya.k: two options: 1) enable proxy_protocol support in ingress (envoy/nginx accept proxy v2) so PROXY is consumed before TLS parsing, or 2) disable proxy_protocol on the target group and rely on X-Forwarded-For from ALB (but then we lose client IPs for mTLS decisions).

sanjay: since we need true mTLS to the backend we should keep passthrough. nginx + mTLS + proxy v2 is the right fix. I'll open a quick PR to enable proxy_protocol on the ingress Service and set the nginx config to `listen 443 proxy_protocol` and `real_ip_header proxy_protocol`.

alex.m: will that work for all pods? double-check kube-proxy / host networking interactions. also need to ensure we only accept v2 header (not v1) - safer.

maya.k: also add an e2e: simple openssl test in the job that connects via NLB and verifies tls handshake success and that first bytes are ClientHello (no PROXY) after the fix.

ryan: temp mitigation: route traffic for the affected customer to ALB TLS termination (we can terminate at ALB and do mTLS-to-backend later once certs validated) — i'll make a routing rule in Route53 weighted policy.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0452 — TLS passthrough failures due to proxy_protocol mismatch. Priority: P2. Assigned: eng-runtime, eng-infra.

sanjay: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/merge/3312 — adds proxy_protocol v2 support and nginx listener change. rolling out to staging now.

alex.m: after deploy to staging, can someone run `openssl s_client -connect <nlb-ip>:443 -servername private.example.com -msg` and paste ClientHello bytes? should NOT show PROXY prefix.

maya.k: staging checks green. openssl client shows ClientHello at start. monitoring: handshake_failures trending down in eu-west-1.

alex.m: thanks team. follow-up: add a small detection alert that fires if first TCP payload contains ASCII "PROXY" when port is 443 — will catch config drift.

ryan: added detection rule: tcp_first_payload_contains_proxy -> alert to eng-runtime. :white_check_mark:

sanjay: will backport nginx change to older clusters and schedule a maintenance window for production rollout with minimal traffic shift plan.

alex.m: closing thread once prod rollout done. great catch everyone :tada:
